name: Premium multi-styler

lead: A premium multi-styler is a hair tool with swappable heads that can dry, curl, smooth and add volume. The best-known example is the Dyson Airwrap, and several competitors now sell similar devices. The payoff is a polished, voluminous style from one tool, visible immediately.

The device blows heated air through attachments that wrap, brush or shape the hair. Makers say the airflow lets them style at lower heat than traditional irons; that is a manufacturer claim and no independent trial of it has been published.

paras: People use the attachments to dry, then curl or smooth in sections, often as a replacement for a dryer plus curling iron. The look lasts until the hair is next washed or restyled.

As with other heated tools, burns and heat-related hair damage are possible. It is sold as a consumer appliance with no medical regulation, and prices are high. Rival makers have been involved in patent disputes with Dyson.

angle.text: A multi-styler such as the Dyson Airwrap dries, curls, smooths and adds volume with one device, for a polished look that is visible immediately. Makers say airflow styling uses less heat than irons; no independent trial has tested this.

lead: A premium multi-styler is a high-priced, multi-attachment hair tool that combines drying, curling, smoothing and volumising functions in one device. People use it to get salon-style curls, waves, smooth ends or volume at home, which changes how full and polished hair looks for the day. The category is most closely associated with the Dyson Airwrap, made by the British appliance company Dyson, which also sells hair dryers and other styling tools.[1]

The tools are discussed as a way to shape hair with airflow and interchangeable attachments rather than only clamping hair between hot plates, as a conventional curling iron or flat iron does. Manufacturers make claims about heat exposure for their own designs; no published clinical trial of a multi-styler's effect on hair condition or styling outcome was found.
Competing products from other manufacturers have followed. In 2023 Dyson sued SharkNinja over a patent related to a hair styler, seeking to block sales of the Shark FlexStyle air-styler range.[1]

paras: A multi-styler is a single handle and motor unit that accepts several interchangeable heads, such as curling barrels, smoothing brushes and drying nozzles. The category is positioned as a premium alternative to separate hair dryers, curling irons and straighteners. Dyson's company page describes the firm as making hair dryers and other hair-styling tools, and names the Dyson Airwrap in a 2026 ambassador campaign.[1] Dyson's high-speed motors, developed for vacuums and hand dryers, are described in a list of the company's products, which notes a motor version used in its hair dryer.

Wikipedia's hair iron article explains that heat from styling tools can break the hydrogen bonds in the hair's cortex so the hair takes a new shape, and that the bonds can re-form when the hair meets moisture, so the style may relax.[2] This is why heat-styled shapes are temporary.

Dyson has a history of patent disputes with SharkNinja. In 2023 it sued over a hair-styler patent, seeking an injunction against Shark FlexStyle air stylers and their attachments; the company page does not report an outcome.[1]

No looksmaxxing forum material on this product category was found. Hair styling tools in general are treated in appearance communities as part of hair presentation rather than as a way of changing facial structure or hair growth.

Heated styling tools of all kinds carry the general risks of burns and, with repeated high heat, hair-shaft damage. Wikipedia's hair straightening article says hot tools can permanently change hair's structure if the heat is too high or applied too long, and that heat protectant products can reduce this harm.[3] Manufacturers state that their designs aim to reduce heat damage; no independent published study of these claims was found.

timeline.event: Dyson brings a patent infringement suit against SharkNinja over an air-styling hair tool.[1]
